title: Guides
desc: Choose the PHPRegex integration that fits your workflow: PHPStan, Psalm, Rector, PHPUnit, Infection, Laravel, Symfony, the language server, or the CLI.

title: CLI Guide
desc: Install the PHPRegex CLI and drive it end to end: parse, explain, analyze and lint patterns, with every option, exit code, output format and CI recipe.

title: Formatting Patterns
desc: Lay a long regex out over lines under x, or compact a laid-out one to a single line, with the guarantee that the result matches exactly what the input matched.

title: Infection
desc: Infection mutators for the regex literals of preg_*() calls: no mutant the automata prove equivalent to the original, and each mutant with the subject that kills it, ready to paste into a test.

title: Laravel Guide
desc: Wire PHPRegex into a Laravel 10.37 to 13 app: the Regex service and facade, the regex:* artisan commands, lint targets, ReDoS findings and the 1.x upgrade.

title: LSP Integration Guide
desc: Point any LSP editor at the PHPRegex language server: install it, configure VS Code, PhpStorm, Neovim or Zed, pick its target PHP and PCRE2, and debug it.

title: MCP Server Guide
desc: Give a coding agent the regex judgement of PHPRegex over the Model Context Protocol: install the server, wire it into Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Zed or VS Code, read what each tool answers, and debug it.

title: PHPStan
desc: Install the PHPRegex PHPStan extension: the invalid-for-target check that runs by default, plus lint, ReDoS and optimization checks on demand.

title: PHPUnit
desc: The PHPRegex PHPUnit assertions: assert what a pattern captures with exact capture semantics, that the running engine compiles it, and that it is proven linear — with group names validated against the pattern itself.

title: Psalm
desc: The PHPRegex Psalm plugin: how $matches gets the shape of the pattern, what the plugin leaves to Psalm, and the PHP version patterns are judged for.

title: Rector
desc: PHPRegex Rector rules that turn a preg_* call into the string function the automata prove equivalent: sets, single rules, and what each rewrite proves.

title: ReDoS Guide
desc: How PHPRegex proves a regex safe from ReDoS or hands you the attack that kills it: verdicts, witnesses, confirmed mode, and the fixes that keep patterns linear.

title: Regex in PHP
desc: A PHP regex primer: how PCRE2 powers preg_match(), delimiters, flags, limits and common mistakes, plus the PHPRegex calls that analyze each pattern.

title: Symfony Bundle Guide
desc: Register the PHPRegex bundle in Symfony 6.4, 7.4 or 8.x: the php_regex.regex service, regex:* console commands, route and firewall analysis, the 1.x upgrade.

title: Maintainers Guide
desc: Embed PHPRegex in your own tool: configuration options, the exception surface, machine-readable lint JSON for CI gates, and the wrapper and visitor integration patterns.

title: AST Node Reference
desc: Every AST node type in PHPRegex with its fields and runnable examples — groups, quantifiers, classes, verbs — and the position rules all nodes share.

title: Choose a package
desc: Choose the PHPRegex package that matches your task: parsing, application API, CLI, static analysis, editor integration, or a framework bridge.

title: Privacy
desc: What php-regex.com measures, and what it never sees: Google Analytics counts visits with its cookies, and nothing you type in the playground leaves your browser.

title: Quick Start
desc: Install PHPRegex and run your first regex analysis in five minutes with the CLI or the PHP API.

title: Reference Index
desc: Find the PHPRegex reference page you need by task: diagnostics, compatibility, programmatic data, or background material.

title: API Reference
desc: The PHPRegex facade — Regex::create() and every method, validate to transpile — with executed examples, result objects and the exception map.

title: Backward Compatibility Promise
desc: What a PHPRegex minor or patch release may change, what stays for all of 2.x, and what only the next major release may touch.

title: Capture Shapes
desc: What CaptureShapeAnalyzer reads from a pattern alone: which groups every match sets, their values, lengths and facts, and the $matches type it writes.

title: Safety and Correctness Contracts
desc: The formal guarantee of each PHPRegex analysis — parser, lint, optimizer, the ReDoS model, the automata solver — sound, complete or best-effort.

title: Diagnostics Cheat Sheet
desc: One fix per common PHPRegex diagnostic: unbounded lookbehinds, bad backreferences, nested quantifiers, useless flags and delimiter traps.

title: Diagnostics and Error Messages
desc: How PHPRegex reports errors: validation layers, ValidationResult fields, CLI and JSON output, error-code categories and the fixes for each diagnostic.

title: Extraction Coverage
desc: Which calls each PHPRegex tool reads a regex pattern from: regex lint with and without nikic/php-parser, the language server, the PHPStan and Psalm extensions, and the Laravel and Symfony regex:lint commands.

title: FAQ and Glossary
desc: Short answers to common PHPRegex questions — CI integration, caching, exceptions — plus a glossary of the terms used across the documentation.

title: Feature Support Matrix
desc: Which PCRE constructs each PHPRegex layer reads: the parser, the lint and optimizer rules, the ReDoS model, and the automata solver's regular subset.

title: JSON Output

desc: Compare two patterns as languages — intersection, subset, equivalence, prefix — answered on a DFA built from the pattern, with the engine's own character sets.

title: Pattern Info and Compatibility
desc: The facts PatternInfo reads from a pattern — capture counts, names, limits, anchors, match lengths, a sure match — and the PHP and PCRE2 versions it is valid on.

title: Prefilters

title: External References
desc: The external sources PHPRegex trusts: PCRE2 and PHP manuals, ReDoS references, engine theory, testers and Unicode standards.

title: PHPRegex Rule Reference
desc: Every PHPRegex lint rule — when each fires, its message, its severity and its fix — from flags and anchors to ReDoS and Unicode byte traps.

title: SonarPHP Regex Rules
desc: The PHPRegex identifier behind each of SonarPHP's 25 regex rules — covered, covered in part, or out of scope — for teams moving from Sonar or running both.

title: Troubleshooting Guide
desc: Fixes for the errors PHPRegex actually prints: lexer messages, ReDoS verdicts, cache and memory issues, CLI and Symfony bridge problems.

title: Regex Tutorial
desc: Learn regular expressions from scratch, step by step — with clear examples, exercises, and PHP `preg_match()` along the way.

title: Chapter 1: Regex Basics
desc: Learn what a regex pattern is, match literal text, understand delimiters and escaping — with no prior regex knowledge required.

title: Chapter 2: Character Classes & Escapes
desc: Match sets of characters with [abc], ranges, negation, shorthand classes like \d and \w, and when to use them.

title: Chapter 3: Anchors & Boundaries
desc: Control where a match can happen with anchors (^, $, \A, \z) and word boundaries (\b).

title: Chapter 4: Quantifiers & Greediness
desc: Control repetition with *, +, ?, and {n,m} — and understand greedy vs lazy matching.

title: Chapter 5: Groups & Alternation
desc: Group patterns with (...), use alternation with |, and learn capturing, non-capturing, and named groups.

title: Chapter 6: Lookarounds & Assertions
desc: Match context without consuming it with lookaheads and lookbehinds — positive and negative.

title: Chapter 7: Backreferences, Subroutines & Recursion
desc: Reuse captured text with backreferences, and see how subroutines and recursion work for more advanced patterns.

title: Chapter 8: Performance & ReDoS
desc: Understand catastrophic backtracking, spot risky patterns, and write safer ones.

title: Chapter 9: Testing & Debugging
desc: Learn a simple way to test and debug regex patterns using plain PHP first.

title: Chapter 10: Real-World Patterns in PHP
desc: Practical regex patterns for everyday tasks in PHP.

title: AST Visitor Reference
desc: The built-in PHPRegex visitors — print, rewrite, modernize, validate, explain, render — each with its real output, and the base classes to extend for your own.
